2.
The Petitioner shall file legible and clearer copies of exempted documents, compliant with practice rules, before the next date of hearing.
3. Accordingly, the applications stand disposed of.

The present petitions under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, 1950 read with Section 528 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 seek writ in the nature of mandamus, directing Respondent No. 2 to renew their Passports pending the proceedings arising out of FIR No. 58/2015 dated 18th January, 2015 registered at P.S. Preet Vihar for the offence under Sections 420/465/467 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.1 Both the Petitioners have been released on bail in the said case.

5. The Petitioners submit that they had submitted applications for the renewal of their passports;
however, their requests were not processed, and they were instructed to obtain permission from the Court to allow them to travel abroad.
The Petitioners clarify that, at this juncture, their applications are solely for the renewal of their passport, and they have no intention of traveling abroad at present.

They further submit that, in any case, should they wish to travel abroad once their passports are issued, they will duly seek authorization from the relevant Court, in light of the restrictions placed "IPC"
This is a digitally signed order.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 12/04/2025 at 01:51:54 upon them as part of their bail conditions.

6. Ms. Nidhi Raman, CGSC for Respondent Nos. 1 to 3, argues that the said restriction is pursuant to the Office Memorandum bearing GSR 570(E) dated 25th August, 1993, issued by the Ministry of External Affairs/ Respondent No. 2.
7.

Counsel for the Petitioners argues that this condition should not be enforced, as there is no provision within the Passports Act that grants the passport office the authority to require Court permission for departure from India.
He asserts that the OM cited by the Respondent is both arbitrary and ultra vires.
Accordingly, he states that he would also apply for an amendment of the petitions, seeking quashing of the aforesaid OM.
8. Be that as it may, in the opinion of the Court, the Petitioners' contention has merit.
9. Issue notice.
Counsel appearing for the Respondents mentioned above accept notice.
